dossier.public_summary: The dip looks planet-sized and flat-bottomed, but the measured depth jumps from a few hundred parts-per-million to over 7,000 ppm between sectors and between individual transits, with just a couple of extremely deep events creating the signal. That variability is inconsistent with a stable planet on this small M-dwarf and favours noise/systematics. The best explanation is not a planet on the target.

reasons.why: Individual transit depths are wildly inconsistent (chi2 123.78 dof 13). The top 3 carry 0.88 of signal and coincide with 1-2 extreme outliers, inconsistent with a persistent planet transit.
Sector depths change far beyond errors: 1504 ppm sector 24, 423 ppm sector 25, 5897 ppm sector 52, 7869 ppm sector 78 (depth_change_pct 189.8).

The variation is not a calibration offset; SPOC alone shows p_constant 5.036394758389399e-11, so depth truly changes with time/observing conditions as expected for systematics or systematics-contaminated detections and not for a steady planet on this M dwarf.

Low planet rank below 0.1, typical of false positives when a few bad transits drive the detection (here SNR 10.46 refit SNR 10.22 but dominated by outliers). Flat shape (shape.v_sigma -0.1043) and no secondary (secondary.snr 2.179) and no on-target neighbour (plausible_within_1px 0) do not outweigh the positive evidence of depth-instability and outlier-driven signal.
